# Rendering

## Anti-Aliasing

#### Anti-Aliasing Method { #unreal-cvar-r-antialiasingmethod }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>TSR</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:cvar:r:AntiAliasingMethod</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealcvarrAntiAliasingMethod_bobeb</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Engine default (project setting) for AntiAliasingMethod is (postprocess volume/camera/game setting still can override) 0: off (no anti-aliasing) 1: Fast Approximate Anti-Aliasing (FXAA) 2: Temporal Anti-Aliasing (TAA) 3: Multisample Anti-Aliasing (MSAA, Only available on the desktop forward renderer) 4: Temporal Super-Resolution (TSR, Default) 5: Subpixel Morphological Anti-Aliasing (SMAA) Console variable r.AntiAliasingMethod (process-wide).

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="ref-anti-aliasing"></div>

| Value | Label |
|---|---|
| `0` | None |
| `1` | FXAA |
| `2` | TAA |
| `4` | TSR |

#### Screen Percentage { #unreal-cvar-r-screenpercentage }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>100</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>10 to 200</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:cvar:r:ScreenPercentage</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealcvarrScreenPercentage_1kbeb</code></dd></div></dl>

To render in lower resolution and upscale for better performance (combined up with the blenable post process setting). 70 is a good value for low aliasing and performance, can be verified with 'show TestImage' in percent, \>0 and \<=100, larger numbers are possible (supersampling) but the downsampling quality is improvable.\<=0 compute the screen percentage is determined by r.ScreenPercentage.Default cvars. Console variable r.ScreenPercentage (process-wide).

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="ref-screen-percentage"></div>

#### Lower Resolution While Moving { #unreal-cvar-r-hdue-interactiveresolution }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>On</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:cvar:r:HdUE:InteractiveResolution</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealcvarrHdUEInteractiveResolution_pzbebe</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Interactive hosts (Houdini's viewport): render at Moving Screen Percentage while the camera or scene changes, and at full Screen Percentage 250 ms after the last change. Realtime mode only. Console variable r.HdUE.InteractiveResolution (process-wide).

#### Moving Screen Percentage { #unreal-cvar-r-hdue-interactivescreenpercentage }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>50</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>10 to 100</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:cvar:r:HdUE:InteractiveScreenPercentage</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealcvarrHdUEInteractiveScreenPercentage_h9bebe</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Screen percentage while moving, upsampled by the anti-aliasing method (TSR by default). Console variable r.HdUE.InteractiveScreenPercentage (process-wide).

#### NVIDIA DLSS { #unreal-cvar-r-ngx-dlss-enable }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>Off</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:cvar:r:NGX:DLSS:Enable</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealcvarrNGXDLSSEnable_5fbebde</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span><span class="hdue-badge">Advanced</span></dl>

NVIDIA DLSS Super Resolution in place of TAA or TSR: Screen Percentage picks the DLSS mode, 100 is DLAA. Needs NVIDIA's DLSS plugin in the backend (docs/building.md) and an RTX GPU; otherwise the anti-aliasing method renders. Realtime mode only. Console variable r.NGX.DLSS.Enable (process-wide).

#### DLSS Ray Reconstruction { #unreal-cvar-r-hdue-dlss-rayreconstruction }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>Off</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:cvar:r:HdUE:DLSS:RayReconstruction</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealcvarrHdUEDLSSRayReconstruction_pzbebee</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span><span class="hdue-badge">Advanced</span></dl>

NVIDIA DLSS Ray Reconstruction: DLSS also denoises, in place of UE's denoisers (Lumen reflections, ray traced shadows), through the DLSS plugin's own switch, which turns them off and restores them. Needs NVIDIA DLSS on. Realtime mode only. Console variable r.HdUE.DLSS.RayReconstruction (process-wide).

## Path Tracing

#### Max. Bounces { #unreal-postprocess-pathtracingmaxbounces }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>32</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 100</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:postProcess:PathTracingMaxBounces</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealpostProcessPathTracingMaxBounces_y2bl</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Path Tracer only</span></dl>

Sets the path tracing maximum bounces. Counts scattering events along a path: 0 shows only emission seen directly, 1 is direct light alone, N matches Karma's Diffuse Limit N - 1. One limit covers diffuse, specular, refraction and volume bounces.

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="ref-pt-max-bounces"></div>

#### Max Path Intensity { #unreal-postprocess-pathtracingmaxpathintensity }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>24</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>1 to 65504</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:postProcess:PathTracingMaxPathIntensity</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealpostProcessPathTracingMaxPathIntensity_qdcl</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Path Tracer only</span></dl>

Sets the maximum intensity of indirect samples to reduce fireflies. Lowering this value reduces noise at the expense of accuracy. Increasing it is more accurate but may lead to more noise.

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="tut-noise-fireflies"></div>

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>On</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:postProcess:PathTracingEnableReferenceDOF</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealpostProcessPathTracingEnableReferenceDOF_zgcl</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Path Tracer only</span></dl>

#### Reference Atmosphere { #unreal-postprocess-pathtracingenablereferenceatmosphere }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>Off</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:postProcess:PathTracingEnableReferenceAtmosphere</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealpostProcessPathTracingEnableReferenceAtmosphere_escl</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Path Tracer only</span></dl>

#### Approximate Caustics { #unreal-cvar-r-pathtracing-approximatecaustics }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>On</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:cvar:r:PathTracing:ApproximateCaustics</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealcvarrPathTracingApproximateCaustics_u7bebl</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Path Tracer only</span><span class="hdue-badge">Advanced</span></dl>

When true, the path tracer will approximate caustic paths to reduce noise. This reduces speckles and noise from low-roughness glass and metals. Console variable r.PathTracing.ApproximateCaustics (process-wide).

## View Mode

#### Debug View { #unreal-debugview }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>Lit</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:debugView</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealdebugView_i0a</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span><span class="hdue-badge">Advanced</span></dl>

Renders one of UE's viewport view modes instead of the lit image, as its View Mode menu does: GBuffer channels, Nanite triangles and clusters, the Lumen scene and surface cache, Virtual Shadow Map pages (with Virtual Shadow Maps on). Nanite views show Nanite meshes: the viewport's, and native Nanite assets. Buffer views are linear data; the others are display-referred, like the Unreal Tonemapper's output. Realtime beauty only: AOVs are unaffected.

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="debug-views-modes"></div>

## Geometry

#### Subdivision Level { #unreal-subdivisionlevel }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 5</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:subdivisionLevel</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealsubdivisionLevel_wcb</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Advanced</span></dl>

Uniform refinement of catmullClark and loop meshes; each level has 4x the faces. 0, UE's USD Stage default, renders the cage; 3 matches Karma's surfaces closely.

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="subdivision"></div>

#### Require Nanite { #unreal-requirenanite }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>Off</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:requireNanite</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealrequireNanite_06a</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Advanced</span></dl>

Meshes from the native asset catalog must render with Nanite (their cooked asset needs Nanite data). Meshes built from Hydra are unaffected.

#### Nanite Triangle Threshold { #unreal-nanitetrianglethreshold }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>1000000</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 10000000</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:naniteTriangleThreshold</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealnaniteTriangleThreshold_bob</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Advanced</span></dl>

Meshes with at least this many triangles build Nanite data, as UE's USD Stage Actor decides (its Nanite Triangle Threshold, default 1,000,000); smaller ones stay regular static meshes, which ray tracing (the Path Tracer, Lumen hit lighting) traces at full resolution. Instancer prototypes always build Nanite. 0 makes every mesh Nanite.

#### Cull Backface { #unreal-cullbackface }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>On</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:cullBackface</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealcullBackface_e5a</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Advanced</span></dl>

Meshes whose USD doubleSided is off render their front faces only, as UE's USD importer does. Off, every mesh renders both sides, as in Karma.

#### Stage Up Axis { #unreal-upaxis }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>Y</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:upAxis</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealupAxis_mva</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Advanced</span></dl>

Overrides the stage's upAxis metadata.

| Value | Label |
|---|---|
| `Y` | Y |
| `Z` | Z |

## Materials

#### Cooked MaterialX Library { #unreal-materialxlibrary }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>(empty)</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:materialxLibrary</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealmaterialxLibrary_wcb</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Advanced</span></dl>

library.json of MaterialX materials cooked to UE materials (scripts/Import-MaterialX.ps1). Unset: HDUE_MATERIALX_LIBRARY, else the runtime profile's materialx_library. Houdini's viewport and husk render the bound MaterialX materials as their cooked assets; a material changed since its import fails a husk frame.

#### Prepared Substrate Library { #unreal-substratelibrary }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>(empty)</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:substrateLibrary</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealsubstrateLibrary_wcb</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Advanced</span></dl>

library.json of prepared Substrate materials (scripts/Prepare-Substrate.ps1). Unset: HDUE_SUBSTRATE_LIBRARY, else the runtime profile's substrate_library. Houdini's viewport and husk render Substrate Builder materials as their prepared assets; a graph changed since its preparation fails a husk frame.

#### Prepare Edited Materials { #unreal-substrateautoprepare }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>On</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:substrateAutoPrepare</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealsubstrateAutoPrepare_fjb</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Advanced</span></dl>

Substrate Builder materials missing from the Prepared Substrate Library, and MaterialX materials hdUE cannot translate at render time, are prepared in the background (UE's editor compiles or imports them, seconds per job) and render once ready: in Houdini's viewport as you edit, and in husk before the frame renders. Off, such a Substrate Builder material shows the library's message and fails a husk frame; such a MaterialX material renders with the inputs hdUE cannot translate at their constants.
